result.title: Scalar Tuned Lens Summaries Offer Limited Incremental Value for Mid-Generation Abstention
result.summary: Mid-generation abstention aims to stop an unpromising response before spending its remaining computation budget. Intermediate transformer states may help predict eventual correctness, but whether scalar summaries of their vocabulary predictions add useful evidence is less clear. We compare Tuned Lens entropy and divergence features with final-state and raw intermediate-state probes under matched, causal evaluation. Across eight instruction-tuned models on MATH-500, raw intermediate states improve ranking, whereas scalar-only probes usually trail the final-state baseline. Scalar hybrids have positive exceptions, but their advantage over position-matched permutation controls is small. Cross-fitted residual comparisons further show that gains over a final-state probe need not require aligned scalar features. Actual stopping runs on two model sizes and two benchmarks reveal a separate accuracy--computation trade-off, with token savings overstating wall-time savings for scalar policies. The evidence supports a restricted empirical conclusion about these scalar features, not a general negative claim about intermediate representations.

AI.brief_summary: 论文在八个指令微调模型上，以匹配的因果评测比较 Tuned Lens 熵/散度等标量摘要、最终状态探针与原始中间状态探针在生成中途弃答中的预测价值，并在两个模型规模和基准上实际执行停止策略，分析准确率—计算量权衡。
AI.relevance_reason: 直接关联 STOP 决策与动态计算：其核心发现是原始中间状态更利于排序，而标量 lens 特征的增量优势较弱，且 token 节省会高估 wall-time 收益；这些证据可供核查中途停止所用内部信号与成本评价，但作者明确限定为对标量特征的实证结论。
